note: When two clauses describe one happening. The saved diagnosis is explicit that even same-item wording can coexist with a distinct transfer, so item identity can never license a merge (CONTRACT C1, CORE-STATUS F3). Evidence kinds are weighed together; none of them is a precondition for computing the others, which is what the earlier prefix-first gate chain got wrong (F1). An unsatisfied link is kept as same_event_candidate, never discarded and never promoted.

records.label: explicit_event_reference
records.note: 그 전달 names the earlier happening. One cue among several, deliberately not a gate.

records.label: unique_prior_event_of_same_action
records.note: If two earlier events share the action, the continuation is genuinely ambiguous and this cue is absent, so the link stays a candidate.

records.label: compatible_roles_no_conflict
records.note: A role pair counts as a conflict only when the two values are decidably different. Where the later value is a pointing expression whose head names no particular thing — 해당 항목 — the pair is undecided, not conflicting: the saved diagnosis shows that reading such a continuation as a different event split the event and suppressed a fact that had already been extracted (CORE-STATUS F4). The identity cues that leave a pair undecided are named here so the decision stays auditable.

records.label: role_value_conflict
records.note: A role pair counts as a conflict only when the two values are decidably different. Where the later value is a pointing expression whose head names no particular thing — 해당 항목 — the pair is undecided, not conflicting: the saved diagnosis shows that reading such a continuation as a different event split the event and suppressed a fact that had already been extracted (CORE-STATUS F4). role_completion.note: A role absent from the earlier event may be filled from the later one only on an accepted link, with a proof citing the earlier event span, the later value span and this policy row. Neither span is replaced (CONTRACT C7).

records.candidate_note: A candidate link still has to be about the same action. Checking a transfer is not the same event as the transfer, however explicitly it names it — that relation is verified_by, not same_event.
records.accept_note: Every accept rule requires an expression that actually points at the earlier happening. The removed rule_identity_and_unique_prior demanded only entity identity, the same action, a unique prior, no conflict and adjacency — every one of which is equally true of two genuinely distinct repeated shipments whose second recipient is simply unstated, and the last of which is satisfied *because* the second clause omits the role. Absence of a contradiction is not positive evidence of identity (CONTRACT C1).
records.prior_count_note: A prior is counted once per clause, not once per surviving reading of a clause, so reading multiplicity can neither manufacture nor remove this cue.
records.uniqueness_note: A referring expression is positive evidence that some earlier happening is meant; it is not proof of which one. Where the same later clause would accept a link to more than one earlier event, every link is kept as a candidate and none is asserted, because the alternatives are mutually exclusive.

records.note: Shared evidence and compatible filled roles support a possible opposing proposition; missing role evidence is not evidence of equality. Preserve support rows for both sides.
